title: The 5-Line Cold Email Swipe File That Booked a $6,000 Branding Client in 11 Days — Plus the Exact Behance Portfolio Mistake That Was Killing Every Reply Before That

tools.name: The 5-Line Cold Email That Booked a $6,000 Branding Client in 11 Days
tools.content:
SUBJECT LINE OPTIONS (pick one — do not overthink it):
• "quick question about [Company Name]'s branding"
• "noticed something on your site, [First Name]"
• "[Competitor Name] just rebranded — thought of you"

---

THE EMAIL (5 lines, plain text, no design, no logo):

Hi [First Name],

I was looking at [Company Name]'s website while researching [their industry, e.g. "independent fitness studios in Austin"] and noticed your brand visuals don't quite match the premium positioning you're going for — [specific observation, e.g. "the logo marks you as budget when your class pricing says otherwise"].

I'm a brand identity designer who works specifically with [their industry] businesses to fix exactly that gap. I recently helped [Client Type, e.g. "a boutique wellness studio"] go from a $1,200 one-off logo project to a $6,000 full brand identity by showing them what the misalignment was costing them in perceived value.

Would it make sense to have a 20-minute call this week? I can show you two or three quick changes that would immediately close that gap — no pitch, just the diagnosis.

[Your First Name]
[Portfolio URL — one link only]

---

FILL-IN CHEAT SHEET:
• [First Name] → decision-maker's first name (find on LinkedIn, not the contact page)
• [Company Name] → exact brand name as they write it
• [their industry] → be specific — "independent coffee roasters," not "food businesses"
• [specific observation] → one real thing you noticed: font, color palette clash, pixelated logo on mobile, stock imagery mismatch
• [Client Type] → a real or anonymised past project — even a $500 project counts if the outcome was clear

---

WHAT MADE THIS EMAIL WORK (the 20% teaching):
It leads with a specific observation about THEIR brand — not a generic compliment. It names an outcome (perceived value gap) they already feel but haven't articulated. It asks for 20 minutes, not a project. That's it.

DO NOT ADD: a portfolio paragraph, a list of your services, your years of experience, a testimonial block, or a 'hope this finds you well.'
tools.instructions: Copy this email word-for-word, swap the bracketed fields for your research, and send it today — do not rewrite it before sending.

tools.name: The Behance Portfolio Audit: The One Mistake Killing Your Replies
tools.content:
THE MISTAKE IN ONE SENTENCE:
Your portfolio is organised like a design school submission (by medium or style) instead of like a sales document (by client result and industry). A prospect in the wellness space lands on your Behance and has to scroll through a tech startup rebrand, a student poster project, and a personal logo exploration before finding anything relevant to them — so they leave.

---

THE BEHANCE AUDIT CHECKLIST:

COVER IMAGE & HEADLINE
☐ Does your profile headline say WHO you help and WHAT you help them achieve — not just your job title?
   ❌ "Graphic Designer | Branding | Print | UI"
   ✅ "Brand Identity Designer for Independent Hospitality & Wellness Businesses"
☐ Is your cover/hero image a brand identity project (not an illustration, pattern, or personal project)?

PROJECT SELECTION (the actual fix)
☐ Do you have at least 3 projects from the SAME industry or client type visible above the fold?
   → If not: reorder your projects so the most relevant cluster appears first, today.
☐ Is every project title written as an outcome — not a deliverable?
   ❌ "Logo & Brand Guidelines — Maple Street Coffee"
   ✅ "How Maple Street Coffee Rebranded to Double Their Wholesale Inquiries"
☐ Does each project description include: (a) who the client was, (b) the problem they had before the work, (c) what you delivered, (d) one result or reaction from the client?
   Template: "[Client] came to me struggling with [specific problem]. We developed [deliverable] to [goal]. The outcome: [result — quote, metric, or next step they took]."

SOCIAL PROOF PLACEMENT
☐ Is there at least one client quote visible inside a project — not buried on a separate testimonials page?
☐ Does that quote mention a specific result, emotion, or decision the client made because of the work — not just "it was great to work with [Your Name]"?

CONTACT / NEXT STEP
☐ Does your profile have ONE clear call to action with a link? (e.g. "Book a free 20-min brand audit → [Calendly link]")
   → If your contact button just says "Contact" and goes to a blank form, fix this first.

---

FAST FIX PRIORITY ORDER (if you have 60 minutes today):
1. Rewrite your profile headline (5 min)
2. Reorder your projects so your best 3 same-industry pieces are first (10 min)
3. Rewrite one project title to outcome format (10 min)
4. Add one client quote inside your top project (10 min)
5. Add a Calendly link to your profile bio (5 min)
→ You now have a portfolio that doesn't kill cold email replies.
tools.instructions: Run through this checklist on your live Behance (or portfolio site) right now — fix every item marked ❌ before you send a single cold email.

tools.name: The 10-Prospect Hit List Builder (30-Minute SOP)
tools.content:
WHAT THIS PRODUCES: 10 real companies with a real decision-maker name, email, and one specific observation about their brand — ready to paste into the cold email swipe above.

TIME REQUIRED: 30 minutes. Set a timer. Do not exceed it.

---

STEP 1 — LOCK YOUR TARGET INDUSTRY FOR THIS BATCH (5 min)
Do not try to target everyone. Pick ONE of the following and commit for this batch only:
• Independent coffee roasters & specialty cafés
• Boutique fitness studios (pilates, yoga, strength)
• Independent skincare or wellness brands (DTC, under $5M revenue)
• Architecture or interior design firms (residential focus)
• Independent restaurant groups (2–5 locations)

→ Write it here: MY TARGET FOR THIS BATCH: ___________________________

(If you freeze here: pick the industry your best past project came from. Done.)

---

STEP 2 — FIND 10 COMPANIES (10 min)
Use ONE of these sources:
• Google: "[city] boutique [industry]" → grab the first 3 pages of results
• Instagram: search the industry hashtag (e.g. #austinpilates) → look at tagged locations
• Yelp / Google Maps: search the category, filter by 4+ stars (signals they care about brand)

QUALIFICATION FILTER — only add a company if ALL of these are true:
✅ They have a website (not just a Facebook page)
✅ They appear to charge premium prices (not discount/budget positioning)
✅ Their logo or brand visuals look noticeably weaker than their pricing/service quality
✅ They have fewer than 50 employees (you want the owner or marketing lead, not a procurement dept)

---

STEP 3 — FIND THE DECISION-MAKER (8 min)
For each company:
1. Go to LinkedIn → search "[Company Name]" → look for: Owner, Founder, Creative Director, Head of Marketing
2. If not on LinkedIn: check the About page of their website — founders almost always have a name there
3. Guess the email using the pattern: firstname@companyname.com OR firstname.lastname@companyname.com
   → Verify free at hunter.io (50 free lookups/month)

---

STEP 4 — WRITE YOUR SPECIFIC OBSERVATION (7 min)
For each company, spend 45 seconds on their website and note ONE real brand problem:
• Logo looks pixelated on mobile
• Stock photography that doesn't match the premium price point
• Inconsistent fonts across homepage vs. menu/services page
• Brand colours that clash with the emotion they're selling (e.g. harsh neon for a "calm" wellness brand)
• No visual hierarchy — everything looks equally important

→ Write it in one plain sentence. This goes directly into the [specific observation] field in your cold email.

---

OUTPUT FORMAT — paste into a spreadsheet:
| Company | First Name | Email | Industry | Specific Observation | Sent? | Reply? |

→ You now have 10 warm, researched prospects. Send the first email today.
tools.instructions: Follow this SOP once to build your first batch of 10 qualified prospects — then repeat it every Monday morning so you are never staring at silence again.

tools.name: The "Should I Send This?" Cold Email Self-Check
tools.content:
Read your draft email and answer each question with YES or NO:

1. SPECIFICITY CHECK
   Does the email mention something specific about THIS company — not something true of every company in their industry?
   → If your email could be sent to 500 people unchanged, the answer is NO. Fix: add the specific observation from Step 4 of the SOP.

2. SUBJECT LINE CHECK
   Does the subject line look like it came from a real person — not a marketing tool?
   → Red flags: ALL CAPS, exclamation points, "Exciting Opportunity," "Following Up" (as first email), "Partnership Proposal"
   → Green flags: lowercase, curious, specific to them ("quick question about Forage Coffee's rebrand")

3. LENGTH CHECK
   Is your email under 150 words?
   → Count them. If over 150, cut the paragraph that talks about yourself the most.

4. ASK CHECK
   Are you asking for exactly ONE thing — a 20-minute call?
   → If you're asking them to "check out your portfolio," "let you know if they're interested," AND "feel free to reply with questions" — that's three asks. Pick one.

5. SELF-PROMOTION CHECK
   Does the email mention your years of experience, your design process, your software stack, or your list of services?
   → If yes: delete it. All of it. The first email is not your CV.

6. PORTFOLIO LINK CHECK
   Is there exactly ONE link in the email — your portfolio URL?
   → More than one link = spam filter risk + decision fatigue. Remove all others.

7. OUTCOME CHECK
   Does the email make clear what's in it for THEM — not for you?
   → Re-read your email from their perspective. If the first thing it communicates is "I want work," rewrite the opening line to lead with the problem you noticed about their brand.

---

SCORE:
7/7 YES → Send it now. Do not revise it again.
5–6 YES → Fix the NO answers (should take under 5 minutes), then send.
4 or below → Go back to the swipe file and rebuild from the template — your current draft has drifted too far.

---

ONE RULE: Send the email the same day you research the prospect. The longer you wait, the more you'll rewrite it into something over-polished that sounds like a marketing email. Done beats perfect — especially in cold outreach.
tools.instructions: Before you hit send on any cold email, run it through these 7 questions — if you can't answer YES to all 7, fix the email first.
